brief_data.deck: UiPath, the New York-headquartered enterprise-automation company, reported on 28 May 2026 the first GAAP-profitable quarter in its history: revenue of $418M, up 17%, ARR of $1.901B and $1.42B of cash, with a chief marketing officer nine months into rebuilding the brand around agentic AI.

risks.label: PROFIT, NOT A RAISE
risks.detail: The trigger is an earnings milestone, not fresh capital; a public company's marketing budget is set on the fiscal-year cycle.
risks.counter: Size the entry to the fiscal-2028 plan now being built; offer platform licences as part of the consideration.

risks.label: CATEGORY IS NEW TO F1
risks.detail: No automation vendor has bought a team partnership; the board will ask what ServiceNow or Salesforce got from theirs.
risks.counter: Lead with the cost-cap workstream: a documented case study is the asset UiPath's enterprise sellers can reuse.

gridfit.detail: no rival in this category lane

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Michael Atalla before the summer break to test the automation lane at Haas against UiPath's fiscal-2028 plan and size an Official Enterprise Automation Partner entry for 2027, announced in Austin.

value.text: UiPath's agents and document-understanding robots handle the paperwork of a 24-race season run from Kannapolis, Banbury and Maranello: customs and carnet documents for flyaway freight, supplier invoices and purchase orders, and the ledger preparation behind the FIA cost-cap submission. The team keeps its people on the car.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: UiPath sells to chief information and finance officers of the Global 2000; its hospitality guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is the audience the team's other B2B partners want to meet.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: A pit-wall-to-back-office story that shows agents doing real work, co-produced with the team; a cost-cap automation case study UiPath's enterprise sellers can reuse; and a US-team platform for UiPath's customer events at the three American rounds.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Enterprise Automation Partner designation, sidepod placement, driver access, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, and a documented operational programme.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 28 May 2026 UiPath reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $418M, up 17% year on year, ARR of $1.901B and GAAP operating income of $28M: the first GAAP-profitable quarter in the company's history. The release is UiPath's own, filed with the SEC, so the figures are VERIFIED rather than reported.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $1.42B at 30 April 2026, the board authorised a $500M buyback in March, and full-year guidance is $1.776-1.781B of revenue with about $430M of non-GAAP operating income. A multi-year team partnership is well inside the marketing budget of a business this size.
why_now.label: Budget exists

why_now.text: Michael Atalla became Chief Marketing Officer on 25 August 2025, hired to position UiPath as the leader in agentic AI and orchestration after the founder's return as CEO. Nine months in, he is building his first full fiscal-year plan; UiPath's fiscal 2028 starts on 1 February 2027, which is when a 2027 partnership would go live.
why_now.label: A CMO with a brand to rebuild

why_now.text: The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American team's home rounds and the two US races left in 2026; teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A conversation opened in June can be sized over the summer and announced in Austin for 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (services), Haas Automation (machine tools), Ruckus (networking) and CommScope on the technology side. There is no enterprise-automation, AI-agent or workflow partner, so Official Enterprise Automation Partner is a clean category. Emburse became the team's travel-and-expense partner in June 2026, so the UiPath workstream is scoped to freight, procurement and cost-cap reporting rather than expenses.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: McLaren, Mercedes and Aston Martin already sell the enterprise-software story at top-tier prices to Workday, SAP and ServiceNow. Haas offers the same paddock and broadcast reach at a team-partner entry point suited to a public company's first motorsport commitment.
why_team.label: The right price point

why_team.text: An American team headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, with three US races (Miami, Austin, Las Vegas) fits a New York-headquartered brand selling to the Global 2000; the Banbury and Maranello sites give the story a European and Italian leg.
why_team.label: Audience and geography

why_team.text: The leanest team on the cost cap is the customer that most needs back-office hours turned into car spend. That is a real reference customer, not a logo, and it is what a documented case study needs.
why_team.label: A team that would use the product

ruled_out.team: Oracle Red Bull Racing · Visa Cash App Racing Bulls
ruled_out.reason: Siemens (industrial software and automation) is a partner of both Red Bull teams; the automation lane reads as taken.
Workday, Alteryx, Smartsheet, Freshworks and Dropbox crowd the enterprise-workflow lane; top-tier price.
ServiceNow, a direct rival in workflow automation, is a team partner.

ruled_out.team: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team · BWT Alpine
ruled_out.reason: SAP and Meta AI at Mercedes; Microsoft (Power Automate) holds the software lane at both.
IFS (enterprise software) and TWG AI are inaugural partners in adjacent lanes.
Atlassian is title partner in work management and Airia holds AI orchestration.
IBM, Genesys and DXC at Ferrari, NinjaOne at Audi, sit in automation-adjacent lanes.

brief_data.bottom_line: A first GAAP-profitable quarter on 28 May, $1.42B of cash and a CMO rebuilding the brand around agentic AI give UiPath the budget and the motive; the automation lane at Haas is open and the two US rounds sit inside the window.

brief_data.the_case_p1: On 28 May UiPath reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $418M, up 17% year on year, ARR of $1.901B and GAAP operating income of $28M, its first GAAP-profitable quarter. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities stood at $1.42B and the board authorised a $500M buyback in March; full-year guidance is $1.776-1.781B of revenue. Founder Daniel Dines returned as CEO in June 2024 and has re-positioned the company around agentic automation: software robots, AI agents and orchestration in one governed system. Marketing sits with Michael Atalla, CMO since August 2025 after F5 and fifteen years at Microsoft.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The enterprise-software archetype is already priced on the grid: ServiceNow sits with Aston Martin Aramco, SAP with Mercedes, and Salesforce is a Formula 1 global partner. UiPath has never held a motorsport position. A first profitable quarter, a founder back in the chair and a new CMO with a brand to rebuild is the moment a public software company can justify a global platform to its board.

brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. The leanest team on the grid runs a 24-race supply chain across Kannapolis, Banbury and Maranello under the cost cap. UiPath's agents and document robots take the paperwork: customs and carnet documents for flyaway freight, supplier invoices and purchase orders, and the ledger work behind the FIA cost-cap submission. Hours saved there are spend redirected to the car. In return: Official Automation Partner status, livery presence, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality.
brief_data.why_team_para: Haas is the grid's American privateer, headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina, with Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner from 2026 and Mphasis, Haas Automation and Ruckus on the technology side. No enterprise-automation, AI-agent or workflow partner sits on the car, so the category is open at a price a first-time sponsor can defend to a public-company board. A US team with three home races suits a New York brand, and the leanest team most needs back-office hours turned into car spend.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Enterprise Automation Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, aligned to UiPath's fiscal years from February 2027. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-deliverable as platform licences. Scope: sidepod placement, driver access, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, a cost-cap automation case study.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The profitable quarter landed on 28 May; a CMO nine months in seat is building his first full fiscal-year plan, and UiPath's fiscal 2028 begins on 1 February 2027. Austin (October) and Las Vegas (November) are the American team's home rounds, and 2027 rosters close in the fourth quarter.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Atalla joined UiPath as CMO on 25 August 2025 from F5, where he led worldwide marketing, after about fifteen years at Microsoft. He owns brand, demand and communications. Path: Daniel Dines, Founder and CEO; Ashim Gupta, CFO and COO.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Michael, UiPath just posted its first GAAP-profitable quarter and you are nine months into rebuilding the brand around agents. No automation company sits on the F1 grid and the lane at the American team is open. 25 minutes before Austin?”
